questions.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution to a Trigonometric Equation Containing Secant or Cosecant
questions.problem: In degrees, what is the general solution to the equation $\sqrt{2}\operatorname{csc}⁡x=2?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation and isolate $\operatorname{csc}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2}\operatorname{csc}⁡x & =2 \\ \operatorname{csc}⁡x & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that $\operatorname{csc}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}.$ Therefore, the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
{x}_{1}=\text{arcsin}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})={45}^{∘}
$$

Our first solution lies in the $1$st quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}={45}^{∘}.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x>0,$ the second solution must lie in the second quadrant, and it also has ${\theta }_{R}={45}^{∘}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14041314/assets/978eaf470ef3b61ff7839471ed4ac46f320922b4d30f7f95566095124d0526d7.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$  lies in the $2$nd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={180}^{∘}-{\theta }_{R} \\  & ={180}^{∘}-{45}^{∘} \\  & ={135}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the given equation is

$$
x={45}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘},\,x={135}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution to a Trigonometric Equation Containing Tangent or Cotangent
questions.problem: Find the general solution to the equation $\operatorname{cot}⁡x=-\sqrt{3}.$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that $\operatorname{cot}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{tan}⁡x}.$ Therefore, the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\operatorname{tan}⁡x} & =-\sqrt{3} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡x & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
{x}_{1}=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})=-\frac{\pi }{6}
$$

The tangent function has a period of $\pi .$  Hence, the general solution for the given equation is

$$
x=-\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi .
$$

Find an expression of the form

questions.worked_solution:
At the intersection points, the $y$-values are the same for both graphs. This gives the equation

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{tan}⁡x=2\sqrt{3} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡x=\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
{x}_{1}=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\sqrt{3})=\frac{\pi }{3}.
$$

The tangent function has a period of $\pi .$  Hence, the general solution for the given equation is 

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{3}+n\cdot \pi .
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution to a Trigonometric Equation Containing Tangent or Cotangent
questions.problem:
Find the general solution to the equation $\operatorname{cot}⁡x=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}-1}$ in the form $x=\theta +n\cdot b$ where $\theta \in [0,{180}^{∘}),$ $n$ is an integer and $b$ is the period in degrees.

*Hint: You may use the fact that $tan\,({157.5}^{∘})=1-\sqrt{2}.$*

$x=$
{{field-1}}${}^{∘}+\,n\,\cdot $
{{field-2}}${}^{∘}$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that $\operatorname{cot}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{tan}⁡x}.$ Therefore, the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\operatorname{tan}⁡x} & =-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}-1} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡x & =1-\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
{x}_{1}=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(1-\sqrt{2})={157.5}^{∘}
$$

The tangent function has a period of ${180}^{∘}.$  Hence, the general solution for the given equation is

$$
x={157.5}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Coordinates of the Points of Intersection of a Trigonometric Curve and a Horizontal Line
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14041314/assets/435dd125850e3f97b5c3753a027f2db8718131ab499ef6711eaac637b1a022bd.png)

The graph shows a portion of the curve $y=2\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and the line $y=1.$ Find expressions of the form

$$
x={\theta }_{1}+n\cdot b,\,x={\theta }_{2}+n\cdot b,
$$

where ${\theta }_{1}<{\theta }_{2},$ ${\theta }_{1},{\theta }_{2}\in [0,2\pi ),$ $b$ is the period in radians, and $n$ is an integer, that generate the $x$-values of all of their points of intersection.

${\theta }_{1}=${{field-1}}$,\,{\theta }_{2}=$
{{field-2}}$,\,b=$
{{field-3}}
questions.worked_solution:
At the intersection points, the $y$-values are the same for both graphs. This gives the equation

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =1 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡x & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find the principal value:

$$
{x}_{1}=arcsin\,(\frac{1}{2})=\frac{\pi }{6}.
$$

Our first solution lies in the $1$st quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{6}.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x>0,$ the second solution must lie in the $2$nd quadrant and it also has ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{6}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14041314/assets/b0738a8a505b89ff687cb4de350a00f2e10d6209fbeee7dcdfdf0ee359a9cc3c.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$ lies in the $2$nd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\pi -{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi -\frac{\pi }{6} \\  & =\frac{5\pi }{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solutions are

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{6}+2\pi n,\,x=\frac{5\pi }{6}+2\pi n.
$$

Therefore, since ${\theta }_{1}<{\theta }_{2},$ we have ${\theta }_{1}=\frac{\pi }{6},\text{ }{\theta }_{2}=\frac{5\pi }{6},\text{ }\text{and}\text{ }b=2\pi .$
